subject: INI-CET Strategy
title: INI-CET Clinical Reasoning: Integrated Questions and Distractors
preview: Integrated exam stems are solved by moving from clinical syndrome to the precise decision asked.

sections.title: Two-step reasoning
points: First choose the syndrome or anatomical localization; next select the specific mechanism, test or treatment decision asked.
Review the negative findings only if they meaningfully change your differential.

sections.title: Practice strategically
points: Use timed mixed-subject sessions, then review errors by concept and source.
A normal test or absent classic sign may not rule out dangerous conditions unless sensitivity supports that conclusion.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Always consult the actual official exam bulletin for current format and timing.
Do not assume every integrated question requires an exhaustive differential diagnosis.

quickRevision: Identify the core syndrome, a key discriminating clue and the requested action or mechanism.
Pathology, physiology, microbiology and pharmacology may appear together in a single stem.
Compare two plausible alternatives using one decisive clinical fact instead of guessing by word length.

quiz.question: How should an integrated INI-CET-style question be approached?
options: Assume all multi-system questions are impossible
Identify syndrome, mechanism and exact task
